key_insight: REST3D reconstructs 3D scenes from a single RGB image while explicitly enforcing physical stability, producing simulation-ready scene geometry that avoids floating, penetration, and other physically inconsistent artifacts.
problem_solved: Existing single-image 3D reconstruction methods often produce geometrically plausible but physically inconsistent scenes (objects floating, penetrating, or unsupported), which break downstream physics simulation and interaction. REST3D addresses this by making physical stability a core constraint of reconstruction.
method: Estimate scene geometry and object-level decomposition from a single RGB image to produce an initial 3D scene.

Integrate physics-aware constraints (e.g., contact/support, non-penetration, gravity) into the reconstruction objective using simulation-informed optimization or learned priors to enforce stable arrangements.
Output simulation-ready meshes/colliders and placements that are collision-free and stable under physics engines for immediate use in downstream simulators.
impact: Makes casual images a practical source of simulation-ready digital assets, reducing manual clean-up and enabling robust AR/VR content creation, robotics scene understanding, and interactive simulations. For practitioners, it bridges single-image perception and physically-grounded 3D asset pipelines.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input photo → geometry & object decomposition → physics module → stable 3D scene
Before vs after comparison: common failure modes (floating/penetration) contrasted with REST3D's stable reconstruction
Contact/support visualization or stability-score heatmap overlaid on reconstructed scene
Short simulation sequence (GIF) showing the reconstructed scene behaving stably under physics
paper_title: REST3D: Reconstructing Physically Stable 3D Scenes from a Single Image
paper_authors: Xiaoxuan Ma, Jiashun Wang, Nicolas Ugrinovic, Yehonathan Litman, Kris Kitani
